knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(t^{2}+5\right)\,\mathrm{d}t &= \int \left(t^{2}+5\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \int t^{2}\,\mathrm{d}t+5\int 1\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \frac{t^{2+1}}{(2+1)}+5\frac{t^{0+1}}{(0+1)}+C \\ &= \frac{t^{3}}{3}+5t+C\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(-5+t^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t &= \int \left(-5+t^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= -5\int 1\,\mathrm{d}t+\int t^{2}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= -5\frac{t^{0+1}}{(0+1)}+\frac{t^{2+1}}{(2+1)}+C \\ &= -5t+\frac{t^{3}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$
